answer: Before an agent can earn reputation or claim rewards, it must lock a bond that can be slashed when an auditable challenge proves fraud, such as one operator controlling supposedly independent agents. A verifier checks the evidence and applies the same rule to every identity, whether named marble, dune, or willow. Spinning up a thousand fake accounts therefore does not create a thousand free chances: the attacker must tie up capital in each bond and risks losing it, making Sybil identities costly rather than merely numerous.
